notes.summary: Current affairs gives about 2 to 4 questions per paper, usually on events of the last 6 to 12 months. This app does not carry monthly news. Take that from one reliable outside source (a monthly current affairs compilation, PIB releases or a national newspaper). This topic gives the method and the stable background every news question leans on: who publishes which index, who appoints whom, where organisations sit, and which events come back every year.

concepts.title: How to study current affairs
concepts.body:
• Use one monthly compilation from a trusted source. Before the exam, revise the last 12 months; papers rarely go further back.
  • Keep notes under fixed heads: national news, appointments, reports and indices, awards, summits, international news, defence, space, sports, obituaries.
  • For every index in the news, note three things: the publisher, India's rank and the top country. Ranks change every year; the publisher does not, so learn publishers from this page.
  • For every summit, note the host city and country, the theme, and the organisation's headquarters.
  • For every appointment, note the post, the person and who made the appointment.
  • For every scheme or portal, note the ministry, launch date and target group.
  • Revise with flashcards once a week; older months fade fastest.
  • Past papers often ask about events from a year or two before the exam, so keep the previous year's notes too.

concepts.title: Recent landmarks (dated, for context)
concepts.body:
• 2023: G20 summit in New Delhi (September); Chandrayaan-3 landed near the Moon's south pole (23 August); new Parliament building opened (28 May); Women's Reservation Act (106th Amendment); three new criminal laws passed.
  • 2024: new criminal laws (BNS, BNSS, BSA) in force from 1 July; elections to the 18th Lok Sabha; Paris Olympics, where India won 6 medals; D. Gukesh became the youngest world chess champion (December).
  • 2025: SpaDeX docking (January); Shubhanshu Shukla became the first Indian to visit the International Space Station (Axiom-4).

Check anything after these dates in your monthly source. Office holders (Chief Justice, Election Commissioners, RBI Governor, service chiefs, heads of UN bodies) change often, so always confirm the current name before the exam.

varieties.name: National news
varieties.how: Note the ministry, date and purpose of each national decision, law or portal. 'First state to' questions are common, so mark firsts.

example.q: In January 2019, which state became the first to implement 10% reservation for economically weaker sections?
steps: The 103rd Amendment (EWS quota) was passed in January 2019.
Gujarat was the first state to implement it, from 14 January 2019.

varieties.name: Appointments and office holders
varieties.how: For each appointment note the post, the person, their earlier post and who appointed them. Use the 'who appoints whom' table for the static half.

example.q: Who appoints the Chief Election Commissioner of India?
steps: Election Commission is set up under Article 324.
The Chief Election Commissioner is appointed by the President.

varieties.name: Reports, indices and rankings
varieties.how: Learn the publisher of each index from the tables here; get India's latest rank from your monthly source. Eliminate options by publisher first.

example.q: The World Press Freedom Index is released by:
steps: It is not a UN index.
It is published by Reporters Without Borders (RSF), Paris.

varieties.name: Awards, summits and events
varieties.how: For every award, note the field, the giver and the winner; for every expo or summit, note the venue, organiser and theme.

example.q: The Global Teacher Prize is given by which organisation?
steps: The prize is worth one million US dollars and honours a teacher each year.
It is given by the Varkey Foundation.

varieties.name: International news
varieties.how: Note the country, the event and the year. For renamed places, learn the old and new names and any later reversal.

example.q: In 2019, Kazakhstan renamed its capital Astana to:
steps: It was renamed to honour former President Nursultan Nazarbayev.
The name went back to Astana in 2022.

varieties.name: Defence and space news
varieties.how: For each test or mission note the name, the agency, the launcher or platform and what is new about it. Link people to the mission they led.

example.q: Who was the ISRO chairman when the Mars Orbiter Mission reached Mars in 2014?
steps: Mangalyaan reached Mars orbit on 24 September 2014.
K. Radhakrishnan was ISRO chairman from 2009 to 2014, covering the launch and arrival.

varieties.name: Sports news
varieties.how: Note the tournament, edition, venue, winner and India's result. Separate one-off events from recurring ones.

example.q: Which Indian naval officer was the only Asian in the 2018 Golden Globe Race, a solo round-the-world sailing race?
steps: The race started from Les Sables-d'Olonne, France, in July 2018.
Commander Abhilash Tomy took part and was rescued after his boat was damaged.

varieties.name: Organisations and groupings
varieties.how: Group headquarters by city and memberships by grouping. For summits, add the host city of the latest meeting from your monthly source.

example.q: Which pair (organisation and headquarters) is incorrectly matched: WTO Geneva, IAEA Vienna, New Development Bank Beijing, ADB Manila?
steps: WTO is in Geneva, IAEA in Vienna and ADB in Manila: correct.
The BRICS New Development Bank is in Shanghai; Beijing hosts the AIIB.

tips: Monthly news is not in this app: use one trusted external monthly source and revise the last 12 months.
Index hook: WEF does gender and risks (and meets at Davos), RSF does press freedom, Transparency International does corruption, WIPO does innovation.
Geneva hosts the most UN-linked bodies: WHO, ILO, WTO, WIPO, ITU, UNHCR.
Development banks by city: ADB Manila, AIIB Beijing, NDB Shanghai.
6 years or age 65 covers the CEC, CAG and UPSC chairman.
Write publisher, India's rank and top country for every index you read about.
traps: UNESCO is in Paris, but UNICEF is in New York.
The IMF and World Bank are both in Washington, D.C., not New York.
The World Happiness Report is not published by WHO or UNDP.
The Global Hunger Index is by two NGOs (Concern Worldwide and Welthungerhilfe), not by FAO.
The Economic Survey comes from the Ministry of Finance, not NITI Aayog or the RBI.

questions.q: Where is the headquarters of the World Health Organization (WHO)?
questions.solution:
WHO is headquartered in Geneva, Switzerland.
Memory hook: Geneva = 'Gene' = health.

questions.q: The Human Development Index (HDI) is published by:
questions.solution:
HDI appears in the Human Development Report of the United Nations Development Programme (UNDP).
Memory hook: Human Development — UNDP.

questions.q: The Economic Survey of India is presented by which ministry?
questions.solution:
The Economic Survey is prepared by the Department of Economic Affairs, Ministry of Finance, and presented before the Union Budget.
Memory hook: Survey before Budget — both from the Finance Ministry.

questions.q: The World Press Freedom Index is released by:
questions.solution:
The World Press Freedom Index is published by Reporters Without Borders (RSF), based in Paris. Transparency International publishes the Corruption Perceptions Index.
Memory hook: Press = Reporters.

questions.q: Which pair of organisations both have their headquarters in Vienna?
questions.solution:
IAEA and OPEC are in Vienna. ILO and WTO are in Geneva; IMF and World Bank in Washington, D.C.; UNESCO and OECD in Paris.
Memory hook: Vienna runs on Atoms and Oil.

questions.q: The Global Innovation Index is published by:
questions.solution:
The Global Innovation Index is published by WIPO, a UN agency based in Geneva.
Memory hook: Innovation → patents → intellectual property → WIPO.

The New Development Bank (set up by BRICS) is headquartered in Shanghai. Beijing hosts the AIIB.
Memory hook: BRICS bank by the sea — Shanghai; AIIB in the capital — Beijing.

questions.q: Which of the following is released by the National Statistics Office (MoSPI)?
questions.solution:
NSO releases the IIP, CPI and the Periodic Labour Force Survey. WPI comes from DPIIT, the Financial Stability Report from RBI, and the forest report from the Forest Survey of India.
Memory hook: Statistics Office counts output, prices for consumers, and jobs.
